title: Coding Set 07: Digital Root & Roman Numeral Validation
description: Reported HCL logic & parsing problems: recursive/O(1) single-digit reduction and strict Roman numeral decoding.

problems.title: Digit Sum Until Single Digit
problems.statement: Given a non-negative integer N (potentially very large, up to 10^100000 digits), repeatedly sum its digits until only a single digit remains, and print that single digit. Solve in O(|digits|) time.
problems.inputFormat: A single line containing non-negative integer N as a digit string.

starterCode.python:
import sys

s = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys

s = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
if set(s) == {'0'}:
    print(0)
else:
    m = sum(ord(c) - 48 for c in s) % 9
    print(9 if m == 0 else m)

problems.timeComplexity: O(D) where D is the number of digits.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra space beyond reading input.
edgeCases: Inputs exceeding 64-bit `long` require string-based digit summing

problems.title: Roman Numeral to Integer with Strict Validation
problems.statement: Given an uppercase string S, validate whether it is a canonical Roman numeral in [1, 3999]. If valid, print its integer value; otherwise print 'INVALID'. Canonical rules: at most three consecutive I, X, C, M; V, L, D never repeat; valid subtractive pairs are only IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM; and values must decrease strictly across tokens (e.g., 'IIX' or 'IXI' or 'VV' is invalid).
problems.inputFormat: A single line containing string S.
